summary: Tested Stripe webhook fix (alert_subscriptions update) and mobile UI changes. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases pass — both /api/payments/webhook/stripe and /api/alerts/webhook/stripe exist, reject invalid/missing Stripe signatures, and the payments webhook source correctly upserts the alert_subscriptions collection on checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated, and customer.subscription.deleted events. Frontend: mobile header shows ALERTS | STRATEGY tabs, clicking STRATEGY loads the ENTRY & EXIT STRATEGY dashboard, and UNLOCK ACCESS sidebar card is correctly hidden for trialing/active users.

minor.issue: On signature failure the handler raises HTTPException(400) inside the outer try/except, which then re-wraps it as 500 'Webhook processing failed' (see except Exception at line 393). Stripe expects 400 for sig errors so it can stop retrying. Add an explicit `except HTTPException: raise` before the broad except.

Same wrapper issue — SignatureVerificationError is caught and re-raised as HTTPException(400) but the trailing `except Exception as e` block returns 500. Returns 500 for invalid signatures (verified: returns 500 in live test) instead of 400.
If STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty the code constructs the event WITHOUT signature verification (testing fallback). This is a security risk in production — guard with an env flag or remove entirely.

Mapping is partial: only sets alert_subscriptions.status (not tier). When Stripe sends status='past_due' or 'trialing', tier in alert_subscriptions is never refreshed. Consider mirroring full status_map used in alert_routes.py.

action_items: In /app/backend/routes/payments.py handle_stripe_webhook(): add `except HTTPException: raise` before `except Exception as e:` so 400 signature errors are not re-wrapped as 500. Stripe needs 400 to distinguish bad signatures from server errors.
Remove or env-gate the no-secret fallback branch in alert_routes.handle_alert_stripe_webhook (lines 234-240) — never accept unsigned webhooks in production.
Consider unifying both webhook handlers (payments + alerts) into a single endpoint to avoid divergent logic (e.g., alerts webhook handles 'past_due', payments webhook does not).
critical_code_review_comments: Two Stripe webhook endpoints exist (/api/payments/webhook/stripe and /api/alerts/webhook/stripe) doing partially overlapping work on db.alert_subscriptions. This duplication will cause drift; consolidate to one endpoint.

payments.py line 393-395 swallows specific 400 HTTPExceptions (signature/payload errors) into a generic 500. Verified in live test — POST with invalid signature returns 500, not 400. Add `except HTTPException: raise` before the bare exception handler.
alert_routes.py L234-240 falls back to parsing the event WITHOUT signature verification when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is missing/empty. Production-unsafe.

In payments.py customer.subscription.updated branch, alert_subscriptions only gets status updated. If subscription becomes 'past_due', tier stays as previous value — keep tier in sync (e.g., set tier='expired' when status in ['canceled','unpaid','past_due']).
test_credentials: mobiletest@test.com / test123456 — verified working (status=trialing, 3 days remaining)
seed_data_creation: None. Tests use static fake Stripe payloads with invalid signatures (rejected as expected) so no DB rows are created.

Tests verify endpoint existence, signature rejection, and that the payments webhook source code contains the alert_subscriptions update logic in all three relevant event branches. The mobile STRATEGY tab and trial-user UNLOCK ACCESS hiding both work as expected. Test user mobiletest@test.com is currently 'trialing' with tier='expired' (odd combination — trialing users may have stale tier='expired' from prior trial end; verify this is intentional). Existing test alerts in DB: 28 alerts for mobiletest user including leftover TESTUI/TESTCOIN entries from iteration 33.
rca of the issue: Original bug RCA confirmed: payments webhook only updated `users` collection. Fix verified by source inspection: handler now upserts alert_subscriptions on checkout.session.completed (lines 227-240), customer.subscription.updated (lines 319-322), and customer.subscription.deleted (lines 343-346). Live signature-rejection works but returns 500 instead of 400 (minor handler bug noted above).
